question.text: The Normans were led at Hastings by this man, who became King of England afterwards and commissioned the Domesday Book.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William the Bastard; or William II of Normandy; accept Guillaume in place of William; prompt on William]
question.clue: This man was son of the Robert I and his mistress Herleva, leading to him being known as "The Bastard."

swap.leadin: This poet's rivalry with John Keats was so intense that he used the poem Don Juan [don JOO-an] to mock him after death, claiming that Keats had died from reading a bad review of his work instead of from tuberculosis.
swap.text: Name this English Romantic poet. Keats was convinced that this nobleman had bought good reviews for works like Childe Harold's Pilgrimage.
swap.answerHtml: Lord Byron (accept George Gordon, Lord Byron; accept George Gordon Noel Byron, sixth Baron Byron)
swap.clue: This commander who, in April 1824, died of a fever in Missolonghi before he could execute an attack on Lepanto.

question.leadin: This war ended with the creation of the Protectorate and the execution of King Charles I.
question.text: Name this war, which saw a clash between factions known as the Cavaliers and Roundheads. The Long Parliament essentially ruled its namesake country during this war.
question.clue: One figure formed a cavalry unit called "Ironsides."

swap.leadin: This woman's ascension rights were restored with the Third Succession Act of 1543, though she and her younger sister remained legally illegitimate.
swap.text: Name this Catholic queen of England who deposed Lady Jane Grey to become queen after the death of her younger half-brother, Edward VI.
swap.clue: Wyatt's Rebellion occurred in protest of this monarch's marriage to Philip II of Spain, during which she experienced several phantom pregnancies.

question.leadin: She was also known as Alexandrina.
question.text: Name this monarch whose reign was the longest in British history until Elizabeth II's overtook it in 2015.
question.clue: This monarch kept Lord Melbourne as prime minister during the "bedchamber crisis" and refused the demands of Sir Robert Peel.

swap.leadin: Name some naval victories for England.
swap.text: Horatio Nelson met his end while leading Britain to yet another victory over the French at this battle of the Napoleonic Wars, which took place in 1805 off the coast of southwestern Spain.
swap.clue: That J. M. W. Turner image of this battle shows the Redoutable and Pierre Villeneuve's flagship Bucentaure in the background behind the looming flagship Victory.

question.leadin: Answer the following about early radicals in British history.
question.text: During this king's reign, the Middlesex By-Election Controversy occurred over whether to seat the radical John Wilkes. This king is more notable for having lost the American Revolutionary War.
question.clue: This king's men put down the anti-Catholic Gordon riots, and his reign contained the Peterloo Massacre and the passage of the Corn Laws under his son's Regency.

swap.leadin: At a crucial point in this battle, Sir William Stanley decided to support the eventual winner.
swap.text: Name this battle fought near Ambion Hill. The Earl of Northumberland's failure to lead his troops into this battle contributed to its outcome.
swap.clue: The winner here later had to deal with uprisings led by the supposed Earl of Warwick and Perkin Warbeck.

question.text: Gerald of Wales, the chaplain to this English king, described seeing an Irish king taking a ritual bath in mare's blood. This king's sons repeatedly rebelled against him alongside their mother, Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine.
question.answerHtml: Henry II [or Henry Plantagenet; or Henry FitzEmpress; or Henry Curtmantle; prompt on Henry]
question.clue: This man became king after the Treaty of Wallingford, which was signed by Empress Matilda, his mother.

swap.text: In England, old tally sticks were regularly destroyed by the holder of this office. The holder of this office traditionally brings a red Despatch Box to Parliament to read a speech on a Wednesday in March.
swap.answerHtml: Chancellor of the Exchequer [prompt on chancellor; prompt on Second Lord of the Treasury] (the day being referred to is Budget Day)
swap.clue: Both Walpole and Churchill also held this economic position during their careers, which sets the inflationary target for British banks and spending limits for ministerial departments.

question.text: In order to honor Albert, Victoria wore her wedding dress at one of these events in 1897, becoming the first British monarch to be given one. The second of these events to occur took place for Queen Elizabeth II in 2012.
question.clue: The prime ministers of eleven colonies gathered at St. Paul's Cathedral to celebrate this event in 1897.

swap.leadin: This man allied with Henry "Hotspur" Percy of Northumberland in a rebellion against the English king.
swap.text: Name this Welsh revolutionary who led a namesake 15th century revolt and is the last native Welshman to hold the title "Prince of Wales."
swap.answerHtml: Owain Glyndŵr (“oh-WINE glin-DOOWR”) [or Owain ap Gruffydd; accept, but glare at and correct, Owen Glendower; accept Glyndŵr Rising or Glyndŵr Rebellion]
swap.clue: After a neighbourly dispute with Reginald Grey, an amnesty was issued to this man's followers by Henry "Hotspur" Percy, who was killed at the Battle of Shrewsbury.

question.text: Skeletons from this Tudor shipwreck suggest that it was crewed by African sailors. After its 1545 sinking, the enslaved Guinean diver Jacques Francis salvaged this carrack warship of Henry VIII, which was raised again in 1982.
question.clue: This sixteenth-century warship, which sank for uncertain reasons off Portsmouth during the 1545 Battle of the Solent, had been the subject of salvage attempts since the sixteenth century, but was finally raised in 1982.

swap.leadin: The last days of this man were described in a journal by Abacuk Pricket.
swap.text: Name this English explorer who sailed under both the Dutch and English flags. He lends his name to a large bay in Canada, which in turn is the namesake of the oldest corporation in North America.
swap.clue: This captain of the Hopewell laid the foundation for the creation of New Netherland through a 1609 exploration.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about rampant crime in Glasgow in the 20th century.
question.text: These turf wars pitted Thomas Campbell against the Marchetti brothers and resulted in Campbell's arrest for the murder of "Fat Boy" Doyle. Its name comes from the vehicles used by Campbell to sell drugs.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the rough-and-tumble world of Anglo-Saxon England.
swap.text: Which king of England, a younger half-brother of Athelstan, was assassinated at Pucklechurch in 946 by the outlaw Leofa?
swap.clue: This descendant of Alfred reconquered Northumbria after Olaf III Guthfirthson invaded it and also restored Louis IV to the throne of France. He also secured an alliance with Scotland by ceding Strathclyde to them after he had conquered it.

question.leadin: Answer the following about medieval European marriage customs.
question.text: Similar to a dowry, this was a payment made by a family to their feudal lord so that their daughter could marry. This practice's name derives from a Welsh word meaning "daughter."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Ælfgyva ("ALF-yee-vuh"), a woman depicted being touched in the face by an unnamed cleric on the Bayeux Tapestry.
swap.text: Some historians have identified Ælfgyva as this queen, who walked barefoot across burning plowshares to disprove adultery allegations. Her husband committed the Saint Brice's Day Massacre.
swap.answerHtml: Emma of Normandy (Her husband was Æthelred II.)
swap.clue: After their first marriage, this figure was given the name Ælfgifu for use in formal and legal matters.

question.text: Erasmus Darwin co-founded this Enlightenment intellectual club in Birmingham whose members included Joseph Priestly and Josiah Wedgewood. Its members were punningly called "lunaticks."

swap.leadin: Sophie's mother is horrified by this event in a section of Jonathan Coe's novel Middle England.
swap.text: Identify this event, the first time that a sitting MP had been murdered since Ian Gow was slain by the IRA in 1990.
swap.answerHtml: murder of Jo Cox [or murder of Helen Joanne Cox; or murder of Helen Joanne Leadbeater]
